newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metallgesellschaft H1 96/97 pretax profit up 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Metallgesellschaft H1 96/97 pretax profit up 50 pct.

text.p: Germany's Metallgesellschaft AG, the diversified engineering and trading group, said on Wednesday that its pre-tax profit for the first half of 1996/7 rose by 50 percent to 106 million marks ($63.1 million).
The firm said that its sales for the same period rose 18 percent to 7.7 billion marks.

"The financial situation of the firm has improved further," Metallgesellschaft said in a statement. It added that for the financial year 1997/98, it expected profits to be above those in the previous year.
MG said that the year-earlier pre-tax profit of 70 million marks was hit by delays in billing plant construction contracts.

MG chairman Kajo Neukirchen held out the prospect of MG -- which has omitted dividend payouts for the last five years -- resuming dividend payouts on the current year's business. Neukirchen told a news conference that if the company met its goal of increasing profits again in the year to September 30 then MG would "intensively consider paying a dividend".
MG ran into huge financial problems in late 1993 due to losses made on U.S. oil deals, forcing it to the edge of bankruptcy. It had to be rescued by banks in a 3.4 billion mark bailout.

Neukirchen told the news conference that the new restructured MG -- now consisting of a holding company and operating units -- was planning to announce the sale of a subsidiary and the purchase of another unit soon.
He gave no details, but added that all of the company's operating areas were currently looking for meaningful acquisitions.

Neukirchen quashed bourse speculation that MG was a takeover target, saying that he was not aware of any attempts to take over the company nor of any major shifts in share ownership among the company's larger shareholders.
